newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Ringgit ends choppy Asian trading lower.
newsitem.headline: Ringgit ends choppy Asian trading lower.

text.p: The ringgit ended a choppy Asian session lower against the dollar after the release of an unexpectedly huge Malaysian trade deficit in April, dealers said.

"It's a roller-coaster ride for the ringgit. Dollar/ringgit jumped to around 2.5170 after the trade deficit news before profit-taking took it back down to just above 2.5100," said a European bank dealer in Kuala Lumpur.
Malaysia announced a trade deficit of 2.1 billion ringgit in April after a 1.75 billion ringgit surplus in March.
Earlier, players covered their short dollar positions as fears the Malaysian central bank would impose capital controls like those of Thailand faded.
A U.S. fund was heard to have bought a fair amount of dollars at 2.5095/00 level in the morning, dealers said.
Offshore players had sold dollar/ringgit aggressively on the capital-control fear on Thursday after Bank Negara called for a meeting with chief executive officers of some banks.
But banking sources said the meeting was to discuss routine foreign exchange activities.
Dealers said dollar/ringgit was likely to remain between U.S. fund buying interest above 2.5080 and corporate sales out of Kuala Lumpur around 2.5180.
At 1000 GMT, ringgit was quoted at 2.5131/41 a dollar against 2.5115/25 at Kuala Lumpur close on Thursday.
